query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled secondary phase (e.g., precipitating a hard magnetic phase such as Fe2O3 or CoFe2O4) into the single-phase fcc FeCoNi matrix via partial oxidation or alloying with oxygen will increase the coercive field above 100 Oe by providing additional domain wall pinning centers.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched single-phase fcc high-entropy alloy derivative
generation.intervention: Partial oxidation or alloying with oxygen to induce nanoscale precipitates of a hard magnetic oxide phase (e.g., Fe2O3 or CoFe2O4) within the fcc FeCoNi matrix
generation.conditions: Controlled oxidation at moderate temperatures (e.g., 300–500°C) in air or oxygen atmosphere, targeting sub-micron/nanoscale oxide precipitate formation while retaining the majority fcc matrix
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale oxide precipitates embedded in the fcc FeCoNi matrix, acting as domain wall pinning centers
generation.mechanism: The precipitated hard magnetic oxide phase increases coercivity by impeding domain wall motion, thereby requiring higher fields to reverse magnetization
generation.predicted_outcome: Coercive field will increase above 100 Oe, potentially reaching several hundred Oe, while saturation magnetization may decrease slightly due to non-magnetic or weakly magnetic oxide phase inclusion
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or matched fcc high-entropy alloy derivative with coercive field ≤ 100 Oe
generation.boundary: Prediction applies to FeCoNi and its fcc high-entropy alloy derivatives; intervention must not convert the matrix to a non-fcc phase or cause excessive oxidation that destroys bulk magnetic properties; oxide precipitate volume fraction should be <20%
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of coercivity increase depends on precipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction; excessive oxidation may degrade overall magnetization; optimal processing conditions are not precisely established

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two samples: (1) single-phase fcc FeCoNi (or matched derivative), (2) same composition subjected to controlled oxidation to induce nanoscale oxide precipitates. Characterize both by XRD, TEM, and measure magnetic hysteresis loops (M-H curves) at room temperature.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the oxidized sample does not exhibit a coercive field >100 Oe (and all other conditions are met), the hypothesis is falsified.
